# David Packer Advises Against Using Heavy Bands For Calisthenics Skills

David Packer advises against using heavy bands for calisthenics skills, stating they create a false sense of progress and people become dependent on them. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]

## Details

- He does not recommend giant bands at all, only light bands when you are close to the real skill. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- People who use giant bands for planche spend a whole year and then vanish, never seen again. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- People who follow skill progressions like front lever pull-ups most of them end up with a result to show for themselves. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- If you spend a whole year using bands for planche, you could be doing handstand push-ups, deep 90 degree dips, and other exercises with your whole body weight. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- He cannot think of any good use for a heavy band of 15 or more kilograms of assistance, except maybe warming up. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]

## Evidence

- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "i don't recommend giant band at all i only recommend like band yeah and that's because one one key thing is that you can spend um and there's so many examples of people posting their you know reverse planche with a giant band and then they just vanish you never see anything from them again"
- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "and then you see all the guys who follow the progressions like you know front lever pull ups p bar whatever most of them end up um you know with a result to show for themselves"
- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "if you're just spending a whole year using bands for planche you could be doing your front you could be your handstand push-ups deep 90 degree hair sample shops you know you're you know you can play with it with your whole body weight"
- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "when i say heavy band i mean 15 or more kilograms of assistance okay um i don't i can't i can't think of any no maybe warming up and then but then you use the light band as well"
